item.text:
**4B.3 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **No**. The 2024 record shows repression, not tolerance, toward protest, dissent, media criticism, and civil-society scrutiny. The only positive material is narrow and procedural: coalition bargaining after a hung parliament and one local call for peaceful negotiation in Azad Kashmir. I found no solid 2024 evidence that Sharif actively protected satire or investigative journalism.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Shehbaz Sharif to be coalition candidate for next Pakistan PM -spokeswoman | Reuters | 2024-02-14 | https://theprint.in/world/shehbaz-sharif-to-be-coalition-candidate-for-next-pakistan-pm-spokeswoman/1965379/ | Weak positive only: after a hung parliament, Sharif’s return depended on coalition bargaining, so power remained procedurally contestable. This is not proof he welcomed criticism or monitoring, but it is the closest pro-tolerance item for opposition victories. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| PM Shehbaz urges AJK govt, political leadership to resolve issues through dialogue | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-12 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-05-2024/pm-shehbaz-urges-ajk-govt-political-leadership-to-resolve-issues-through-dialogue | Narrow positive: Sharif told party and local leaders to negotiate with the Azad Kashmir action committee and resolve the dispute peacefully. That shows some willingness to avoid coercion in a live protest-like flare-up, but it is a localized exception, not a general tolerance posture. | 4B.3, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Clear negative: the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown chilled expression, assembly, and monitoring at a politically sensitive moment. Amnesty treated it as a rights violation, cutting against tolerance for criticism and civil-society scrutiny. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says | Reuters | 2024-04-17 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | Clear negative: the state acknowledged blocking X around the election period on national-security grounds. That directly restricted criticism, reporting, and civil-society communication. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent | Clear negative: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, while media pressure and lack of safeguards deepened self-censorship. This is strong evidence against tolerating criticism or monitoring. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.10 |
| Pakistan: Civil Society Joint Statement Responding to Network Shutdowns and Platform Blocking | Amnesty International | 2024-03-15 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa33/7834/2024/en/ | Negative for tolerance: civil-society organizations jointly protested the X block and election-related shutdowns, showing that monitoring voices were active but being obstructed by state controls. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/ | Clear negative: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded powers to restrict gatherings. This is direct evidence against tolerance for protest and civil-society monitoring. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent | Clear negative: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. That is coercive suppression, not tolerance. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10 |
| Pakistan: Repeated punitive crackdowns on Baloch protests must end | Amnesty International | 2024-07-30 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/pakistan-repeated-punitive-crackdowns-on-baloch-protests-must-end/ | Clear negative: Amnesty described deaths, mass arrests, roadblocks, and network shutdowns against Baloch protesters. This is strong evidence that civil-society protest was met with punishment, not tolerance. | 4B.3, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10 |
| Pakistan: Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/ | Clear negative: Amnesty reported deaths, mass detentions, shutdowns, and a pattern of intolerance toward peaceful opposition assembly. This is the clearest year-end evidence against tolerance of protest and dissent. | 4B.3, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10 |
| USDOS 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html | Clear negative: the report says authorities used PEMRA, network access, and government advertising to suppress media deemed threatening, and issued notices to journalists/Youtubers for alleged anti-state material. That directly undercuts a tolerance reading for investigative journalism and criticism. | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.4, 3B.8 |

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif affirmatively protected satire or investigative journalism.
- The positive side is thin: coalition bargaining after a hung parliament and one peaceful-local-dialogue item in Azad Kashmir.
- On balance, the evidence points to **restricted tolerance**, especially around protest, civil-society monitoring, and critical media.
